mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically each of the last four weeks (-56.6 to -50.3), indicating a steady reopening trend that should continue mechanically into the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact: RETAIL_REC improved every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days despite the observed monotonic weekly improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (23.4 to 20.0) indicates people are spending less time at home, which directly substitutes into more non-essential outings including retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL fell from 23.4 to 20.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks even though RESIDENTIAL continues to decline week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility drops by more than 3 points week-on-week from its current near-flat trajectory, it signals a renewed mobility restriction that will suppress RETAIL_REC within one week due to reduced access to commercial districts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT has been nearly flat around -72 to -77 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week even after a TRANSIT drop exceeding 3 points week-on-week is observed.

mechanism_narrative: The large jump in PARKS mobility (-55.9 to -25.0 over four weeks) reflects favorable late-summer weather driving outdoor activity that substitutes for indoor retail and recreation visits, dampening RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks as the substitution persists.
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS rose sharply from -55.9 to -25.0 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 28 days at the same or faster pace as PARKS keeps climbing, contradicting the substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates a joint return of commuting and work-related trips; when both rise together, the combined restoration of daily routine trip-chaining to retail outlets amplifies RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES improved from -45.4 to -41.3 and TRANSIT from -76.9 to -72.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth rate over the next 4 weeks is no higher than in periods where only one of WORKPLACES or TRANSIT improved, despite both improving jointly here.

mechanism_narrative: The deceleration in GROCERY_PHARM growth (from +4.1 points week-on-week at t-3w/t-2w to only +0.6 at t-0w/t-1w) signals that essential-trip demand is saturating, which historically precedes a plateau in overall discretionary mobility including RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change falls below 1 point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM weekly gains decelerated from 4.1 to 1.1 to 0.6 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to grow at its prior pace over the next 2 weeks even though GROCERY_PHARM growth has clearly decelerated below 1 point weekly.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility reverses and rises by more than 2 points in a single week after its recent decline, it signals renewed stay-at-home behavior consistent with a policy tightening, which will suppress RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL has declined steadily from 23.4 to 20.0 over four weeks, making a reversal a notable signal
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week despite RESIDENTIAL rising by more than 2 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The narrowing gap between PARKS and RETAIL_REC improvement rates, combined with still-deeply negative WORKPLACES levels, suggests that outdoor/park activity is substituting for commercial activity specifically in regimes where workplace reopening remains incomplete; this interaction dampens RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks only while WORKPLACES stays below -35.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -35 while PARKS continues rising week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES at t-0w is -41.3, still well below -35, while PARKS rose sharply to -25.0
regime_hint: partial reopening with incomplete workplace recovery
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days at a comparable or faster rate than the prior period even while WORKPLACES stays below -35 and PARKS keeps climbing.
